utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't have the name of the newspaper, but this communique was published both in Bujku and in Koha Ditore.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was it issued by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was issued by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm wondering if you could provide it to the usher and if we could have it. The version you have, is it in Albanian or in English?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It's in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you by any chance have an English version? Probably not.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, sorry I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That is something that I think we can take care of. I'm wondering if you could provide it to the usher. It could be provided to the parties and translated and perhaps exhibited, since you have read Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. from that.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: However, I need a copy of this document because I still have some parts to read out from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I suggest, Mr. Whiting, that it be copied and the copy there returned to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think that's an excellent suggestion, Your Honour, and perhaps since the witness may want to refer to it in his testimony he could hold on to it for now. We'll copy it at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I could just rise to make a suggestion because it's obvious I think to the Chamber that neither side has this document, which is plainly important, the second communique from the KLA. One wonders whether the witness has others that neither side have seen, and I wonder whether some thought may be given at some stage while the witness is still with us as to making inquiries of him as to what else he has with him, as he plainly has other papers. I apprehend this witness may be with us beyond today, and therefore in light of the court's sitting, beyond the weekend. So there is time for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Topolski. Mr. Whiting, I think you were going down that road as the opportunity presented, but you're invited to specifically inquire about it and see what can be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think that's an excellent -- it's another excellent suggestion. However, I would note for the record that it's not the second communique, it's the Second Political Statement, and there's a distinction between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But maybe we can inquire about this further.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you obviously in addition to your statement to the ICTY, you've brought other documents including the one that you've just described. Can you tell us what other documents you have?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Mainly they are political statements of the period between April and September. I have one document which was sent to the international community. It's of the General Staff of the KLA sent to the relevant institutions of the European -- of the international community. This document shows clearly what was the policy that the General Staff of the KLA followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, Mr. Krasniqi, at the next break would have any objection to those documents being copied so that they can be translated and put into evidence if necessary in this proceeding?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was because of this reason that I brought them here, these documents, to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Tribunal would be grateful if they could be copied during the break, Mr. Krasniqi. You will understand that we have to learn about the philosophy and the workings of the KLA, and these documents would be of considerable use to the Judges if they have relevance to this case. So if we can leave it that Mr. Whiting's staff will take them and copy them during the break and then give you back your originals, we'd be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Honoured Presiding Judge. Amongst my documents there is another document, a speech that I held on the occasion of the funeral of the victims of Likoshan and Qirez. And I believe this document can also serve this Tribunal and I find it also necessary for the work of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Krasniqi. We'll collect those documents and copy them at the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But for now we'll move on and I'm going to draw your attention to communique number 43. In the Albanian it's at U008-1611. In the English it's at 8561, also on the Sanction. It's communique number 43 from the 4th of March, 1998, published in Bujku on page 11. And I believe on the Albanian version it's on the top left of the page. Do you see that communique, Mr. Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was it issued by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to draw your attention just to the end, to the phrase at the end: "Death to enemies and traitors!" Is "traitors" a reference to collaborators?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn now to communique number 45 from the 11th of March, 1998, published in Bujku on page 11. On the Albanian it's at 1612; on the English it's 8566. It's also on the Sanction. And I think it's at the bottom right of the page in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, was that communique issued by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to the first few paragraphs of the communique, and I'm just going to read them out. "In the last few days since 7 March, our armed forces have clashed on a broad front with formations of the occupying Serbian military and police forces and Chetnik volunteers. "Military confrontations stretch across a wide front, extending from Gllogoc [Glogovac] in the direction of Skenderaj [Srbica] in the north, towards Kline, towards Mitrovice in the east, and in the villages along the Cicavice ridge," again forgive me for my pronunciations, "from Gllogoc in the protection of Pristina, including many villages in the Drenoc region. "The UCK's military formations also engaged occupations forces in the Llap region, in the area between Decan, Gjakove [Djakovica], and Kline, and between Malisheve and Rahovec [Orahovac], crossing from the Lumihat region. There were also engagements on a line stretching from Decan to Peje [Pec]." These various operations that are described which occurred apparently between the 7th of March and the 11th of March, when the communique was published, did those in fact occur, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: May I draw your attention to communique number 47.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's -- in the Albanian it's at 1614; in the English it's at 8573. It's communique number 47 from the 13th of May, 1998, published in Koha Ditore on page 6. And I think it's on the top left on the Albanian page, and in English it's on the Sanction. Again, I would remind the Court and the other parties that if you press "Computer Evidence" it comes in most clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was that communique issued by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, at the beginning of the communique it says that: "On the orders of the UCK General Staff, successive operations against the invasion troops were carried out in Operational Zone No. 1, that is, in the operational subzones of Drenice [Drenica], Erenik, Dukagjin [Dugadzini], Pashtrik [Pastrik], and Llap [Lap]. In the course of bitter fighting on the front, the invading forces suffered major human and material losses. Throughout this period, operations were also carried out against Albanian collaborationists, who, despite earlier warnings, did not abandon their antinational courses of action." Did the things described in that passage that I just read out in fact occur?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There's nothing that I can add to this communique except for minor printing errors in the beginning. This is a time after the Likoshan massacre, after the KLA epic of Prekaz. 14 persons were killed in Likoshan, one KLA soldier and two villagers who resisted, themselves, and 11 civilians who were unarmed and who were in their houses. This is a time when the Jashari family, 22 members of this family, were killed. And altogether about 60 persons in the Jashari neighbourhood, most of them civilians, elderly persons, children, and women, unarmed. And of course in this time to a certain extent, this was a deed of those who served the Serb apparatus. And this is a time when mobilisation begins within the ranks of the KLA. It is also a time when except for those who were already organised within the ranks of the KLA, we see also a solidarisation with the population and the army. It is a time when villagers voluntarily take up weapons and defend their dwellings. It is a time of a general mobilisation of the people and the massivisation [as interpreted] of the people is so great and their will to join the KLA is so great that the guerrilla army now becomes a popular army. This extension -- expansion took place on a horizontal level. We have a period when the engagement of the commanding and leadership structures of the KLA are directed in systematisation of the population in the ranks of the KLA. In this time there are actions that are carried out without the knowledge of the General Staff because of the hatred and the dissatisfaction of the population to fight the enemy. I would like also to point out, you Honoured Judges, is that except for the will and the solidarisation of the Kosovo citizens to join the KLA, there was something else that was a moving force for them to abandon their homes and take up weapons. On both occasions, mainly those who suffered were the unarmed; those who were in their homes. What I would like to say is that a part of the Kosova citizens joined the KLA out of fear as well because a citizen was not feeling safe and secure in a market, in home, on the road. So the only support that the population found was in the KLA. It wasn't easy --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: -- for an army with a political organisation of 300 or 400 persons to control and to organise itself after the events in April 1998. So I think we have to look at all the forms, at all the ways, the reasons, that urged these people to leave their homes, leave their families, give up their jobs, to defend their lives, even sometimes their personal lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said that sometimes actions were taken without the knowledge -- were carried out without the knowledge of the General Staff. When that happened, was the General Staff informed of these actions after they had taken place?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The General Staff through these communiques and statements wanted to enhance the confidence of the citizens in its leading body.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if I -- okay. But let me just put the question again which is: After -- you said that actions were taken at times without the knowledge of the General Staff. Was the General Staff to your knowledge informed about these actions after they occurred and then the public was told about them in the communiques? Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The communiques aimed at informing the public of the military actions undertaken at given periods of time in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And just to bring you back, please, to the communique that we started off looking at, which is communique number 47, and specifically to that first paragraph which references operations in various subzones and -- as well as operations carried out against Albanian collaborationists. My question is: Did those operations in fact occur?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Since they have been given to the media and to the public, of course they must have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention now to a sentence which is approximately halfway through and I'll just read it out and perhaps you'll be able to find it. "In a lightning action by our military formations, an operation against the enemy's punitive expeditions on the main road in the operational subzone of Pashtrik was successfully carried out." Are you able to find that sentence?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know what this refers to, what battle this refers to or what main road is being -- is referred to here?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This does not refer to a specific battle, and this to me is not known. What I want to say here is that this was a propaganda material. It's not something that might be used as evidence and less so as an evidence in a court like the Tribunal, The Hague Tribunal is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, maybe you can tell us what you mean by that. What do you mean by it's propaganda material?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I respect the Honourable Judges. I respect all those who serve this process and wish it to be based on relevant facts. I want once again to say here that for me it doesn't make sense for this Tribunal to take such statements and communiques issued by the General Staff of the KLA as material evidence to prove the guilt of someone. I'm repeating it that these were public materials, documents, used for propaganda purposes. The aim of these documents was to increase the respect and authority of the KLA in the eyes of the citizens. It was a material that spoke also about the war we engaged in, to enhance the organisation of this military organisation for the people to believe in it, to join it; and I think we successfully carried out this, our purpose. In other words, for me it doesn't make sense for such propaganda materials to be used as evidence by the Prosecution to condemn someone for something that in one way or another was and is known to the public in general. What were the organisational means, the operational means; what were the means the KLA had to operate in such circumstances of the time that these communiques and statements speak of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krasniqi, if there's a particular passage that I ask you about in any of these communiques that you believe is propaganda, then please tell me and we can inquire about that and have additional evidence about that. But let me ask you another question at this moment. Were you aware of a battle on -- around the Pristina-Peja highway around Lapusnik around the 9th of May, 1998? Were you aware of that battle?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Of course I was, because my village is situated very close to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the sentence that I read a moment ago: "In a lightning action by our military formations, an operation against the enemy's punitive expeditions on the main road in the operational subzone of Pashtrik was successfully carried out." Is that a reference to the battle in May of 1998 or do you know?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I do know what this is about. I also know that Lapusnik and the fighting waged there do not belong to Pastrik zone. They were -- they occurred in the Drenoc operational zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It -- can you tell us to the best of your knowledge -- well, let me take this one step at a time. This sentence then that I read, is it or is it not a reference to the 9th of May battle at Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It cannot be related to Lapusnik. I'm repeating that the distance between Lapusnik and the surrounding zones -- villages were under the command of the Drenoc, not Pastrik operational zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So I'll ask you some more questions about that in a moment. But what then is this sentence a reference to? Or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'd like to give you an idea or a picture of -- to the Honourable Judges that the Pastrik zone comprised municipalities of Malisevo, Rahovec, Prizren, Shale, and Ferand [as interpreted], former Suhareke, whereas the territory we are talking about in Lapusnik it was and is part of Drenoc municipality, which fell under the Drenoc Operational Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand your testimony on that point, but my question is: Going back to Communique No. 47 and this sentence, and if you don't know, just tell me that you don't know. But there's a sentence that reads: "In a lightning action by our military formations, an operation against the enemy's punitive expeditions on the main road in the operational subzone of Pashtrik was successfully carried out." What is that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I already indicated that the Pastrik zone comprises a very vast area. So some action might have taken place in the area of Rahovec municipality in Ferand, Prizren, and in the other part of Malisheve municipality because that was a vast area and the operational units might have carried out some actions in one of these municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the reference to the main road in that sentence, do you know what main road that is referring to?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. There is the Prishtine-Peja road which passes through Carraleve valley and Ferand, but not in Komorane, Lapusnik, Kline and Peja. We have to deal with two roads. It does not specify which of the two roads it is. And after all, it is hard for me now and even then to follow every action that occurred in every part and road of Kosova. We had other duties to attend to at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that the -- Lapusnik is in Gllogoc municipality, and I've probably mispronounced that. Is that the municipality that Lapusnik is in?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what operational subzone was that municipality in at the time in May of 1998 if you know? Was it in one --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This I know. It was part of the Drenica Operational Zone, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was the entire municipality in your view in that -- in the Drenica operational subzone?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Drenica, Skenderaj municipalities, and the larger part of Klina municipality and part of Kastriot Obiliq municipality were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But my question was: Was the entire municipality of Gllogoc in the Drenica zone? Or was that municipality divided --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The entire municipality was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've had another hour and a half now, Mr. Krasniqi. We'll break now and resume at 5 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, first I want to return to you with the assistance of the usher the documents that you provided. Thank you for those documents. We've made a copy of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And for the record, I've provided a copy of the documents to the Defence. And during the long weekend we will endeavour to copy them -- I mean translate them. I provided only one copy to the Defence, but I have an extra one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I just had one last question about that Communique No. 47 that we were talking about before the break. And do you have that in front of you, number 47? It's --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, there in that first paragraph where there's a reference to operational zone number 1 and then there's reference to various operational subzones, in that paragraph is Operational Zone Number 1 referring to the whole of Kosovo or to something else?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It refers to the entire Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to another document, and it is Communique No. 49. It's at -- in English it's at 8577. It will be on the Sanction. In Albanian it is at 1615 and it's on the bottom right of the page in Albanian and it's communique number 49 from the 13th of July, 1998, published in Koha Ditore on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, was that communique issued by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. The Information Directorate of the KLA issued it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you explain for us what the Information Directorate of the KLA was.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was a directorate responsible for informing the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: As spokesman were you in charge of the Information Directorate?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. I was not in charge of it. I think it's a mistake here because informative -- information might be misinterpreted for informative, it's referring to the Albanian. In the English -- it's probably a mistake, probably, in Albanian or misinformation in the way it's written because the meaning is information, public information, directorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, let me put another to you, maybe we can clarify it. Was this communique -- did the General Staff approve of this communique? And I would draw your attention to the end of the communique where it reads: "Thus ends Communique No. 49 of the UCK General Staff." Was this communique approved by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I want to draw your attention to I think it's the third sentence of the document and I'll just read it out. "Measures have also been taken against certain diehard collaborators, who are still working against our national interests. Operations are under way to reinforce and extend the positions under the control of our forces in the subzones of Pashtrik, Llap, Drenice, Karadak, and Dukagjin within Operational Zone No. 1. "Our formations have successfully carried out large-scale operations in the subzone of Pashtrik." Do you see that in the communique?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And is that true? Did those things happen?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'm repeating that this is a propaganda material. If you try to use this material for other ends, I think there is no point in arguing it. We were in a war. We were engaged in a very unequal war. We couldn't tell our people, Come and join us, because we are not organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, we're going to come to some communiques that talk about the organisation of the KLA in a moment, and perhaps that's what you're referring to when you talk about propaganda. But here this refers not to the organisation but to other things. And you have already told us that on -- that at times collaborators were in fact killed. So here my question is -- the sentence where it says: "Measures have also been taken against certain diehard collaborators who are still working against our national interests," is that true? Had measures -- were measures still being taken against collaborators?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me -- excuse me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you could pause a moment, please. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think Mr. Whiting has misstated what the statement is. The statement does not contain the words "measures are still being taken," the statement is "measures have also been taken."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ah yes, that was not his quotation. That was his following question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. My concern is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It followed on earlier questions of earlier times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. My concern is there may have been some confusion with regard to what was being said since he was dealing with the specific statement within the context of this particular communique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith, I don't think this witness is going to be at all confused in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I'll put the question to you again. I'll draw your attention to this sentence where it says: "Measures have also been taken against certain diehard collaborators who are still working against our national interests." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. At this time when this communique was issued on the 13th or -- published on the 13th of July, 1998, was it true that measures were being taken against collaborators?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Distinguished Judges, I think that I have already exhausted this question. I have answered this question and I think that a repetition of the same submissions does not -- will not get another answer from what I have already stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, the questions aren't trying to get another answer from you, but trying to learn whether there has been any change in the position as these different communiques are issued. They span now some months, and that's the purpose, as I would understand it, of the question. So it's not that anything that you've said about this conduct and its justification has been overlooked or is not going to be noticed, but the question is asking: Here is something now published in July. Is this still happening? So if you wouldn't mind with your patience putting up with some repetition as certain matters are made clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I am here to explain what happened more from a political point of view rather than from an operational point of view. However, I want to say that this communique issued by the Information Directorate has to do with more what has happened in the past prior to 13 July 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand that. Is -- however, with respect to -- and if you don't know, then please simply tell me you don't know. But with respect to this sentence that "Measures have also been taken against certain diehard collaborators who are still working against our national interests," do you know if that was in fact true up to that date that up to the 13th of July, 1998, measures were still being taken against collaborators?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'm saying that we have taken measures against the entire violent operators of the Milosevic regime at that time in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you say "the entire violent operators of the Milosevic regime," does that include collaborators?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They were part of the same regime, tools of the same mechanism.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, the next sentence says that -- it talks about -- what appears to talk about military operations that were taken -- or let's say armed operations that were taken by the -- undertaken by the KLA before the 13th of July, 1998, specifically within the subzones of Pastrik, Llap, Drenice, Karadak, and Dukagjin. And there's specific reference to the large-scale operations undertaken in the subzone of Pastrik. Do you know if those operations that are referred to in fact occurred?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Such communiques have to be taken in the context of the propaganda and the specific battles waged in all wars, as the case was in Kosovo war. But until the mid-July, I have to say that not many operational actions were undertaken. They start to be undertaken especially from the second half of July to continue during the entire month of August and September. This was otherwise the well -- notorious offensive waged by the Serb police and army against the Albanian villages during which 70 to 100 per cent of 415 settlements have been razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand your answer with regard to the increase in activity, military activity, that occurred after the -- beginning in the second half of July. But my question is: Before this communique was published, before the 13th of July, were there operations within these zones, as described in the communique? Whether big operations or small operations, did they in fact occur, to your knowledge? If you know.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They happened, but not to the dimensions that the communique says.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. Now, we're going to move on to -- and we're going to move on to Communique Number 51, and this is actually at tab 6. This -- it's at tab 6 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And for the record it is -- the English is a two-page document entitled "Spokesman: UCK is Institutionalized, 'Structured' Army," dated 26th August, 1998, from the Tirana television network," and it's followed by a two-page translation into Albanian. And the English is on the Sanction or let's say part -- the second page of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krasniqi, if you could just take a moment to read this. For this one I don't have a newspaper version of it because it purports to be from the -- transmitted on the television. I see you're looking through the documents that you brought. I myself have not found a newspaper version of it in your document, but feel free to look yourself.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I have a statement here published in Bujku on 28th July, 1998. And this must be it, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On 28 July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: On 28 July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is this -- this article that you have from Bujku from the 28th of July, 1998, is it Communique Number 51?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. This is a political statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. So -- and it's -- is it numbered, the one in Bujku? Does it have a number? It's Political Statement Number --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. The document that I've put before you is -- purports to be Communique Number 51, and it's dated the 26th of August, 1998. So it appears to be something different from the Bujku document which you are referring to. If you could just look at the document that I've put before you. Do you remember that communique, Communique 51, at the end of August 1998? And take your time to read it.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was that issued by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was the time of the August offensive, and fighting was severe in all the zones, the most so [as interpreted] in Drenica and Pastrik, but also in Dukagjin zones. And we consulted on telephone about the situation created. We were informed of the -- from the war zones of what happened and we issued communique of the General Staff that is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I'm going to draw your attention to the last sentence of the communique where it reads: "The UCK is an institutionalised, organised, and structured army, continuously becoming more professional and more prepared to fight until victory."

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. Again, I am referring to what I've said several times. The entire Kosova at that time was engulfed in war and flames as a result of the Serb police and army and paramilitaries led by a command with a sole aim, an aim that was planned from 80 -- 40 [as interpreted]. It was the time when the penetration -- the Serb army had penetrated almost in all the zones controlled by the KLA. At this time I and the General Staff couldn't say that the KLA was disbanded, was not organised. There are some things that really must be looked at carefully, they are -- I'm emphasising it, propaganda, material -- not materials to be used as evidence, nowhere, even as lower-instance courts, let alone at such higher court. These are propaganda materials showing that despite the losses inflicted on it, it's not 415 as it says in the transcript, 450 places were razed to the ground and the international community has seen it through television programmes broadcast on BBC and other television stations which relate news on the burning of the villages in Kosova by the Serb police and army. In a word, as I said, it's propaganda material. After this period, we did, however, manage to go further in our national liberation war and to reinforce ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be Prosecution Exhibit P138.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to show you another communique, it's communique number 53. And for this we go back to tab 1 in English and tab 2 in the Albanian. In the English it's 8606; in the Albanian it's 1616.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I'd ask the usher to assist the witness in finding that in the large format. Usher -- I'm sorry. If you could assist the witness in finding ERN number 1616 in that large format. And on the Albanian page I believe it's at the bottom right. It's published in Koha Ditore on the 19th of September, 1998, on page 2. Was this Communique Number 53 issued by the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I'm going to draw your attention to a phrase that is -- it's about the fifth -- fourth or fifth sentence. It says: "Punitive measures of various kinds are also being undertaken against collaborationist elements that continue to serve the occupying power." And I'm going to put the question again which, again I apologise, may seem repetitive but is important for our understanding. At this time on the 19th of September, 1998, when this communique was issued, were there still measures being taken against collaborators with the Serb regime?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'm repeating that this is a propaganda material, and of course measures were taken against all those who have done harm to the political and military actions of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that would include collaborators?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, in addition to communiques, did you also as spokesman of the KLA give various interviews to the media during this time period in 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did, certainly. That was part of my duties and responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to draw your attention to the document at tab 4 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I'll need the assistance of the usher. And I have -- Usher, I have a large format of that document as well. And for the record the Albanian version is U008-6944 to 6945. The English version does not have an ERN. It's a two-page document entitled "Kosova Liberation Army's TV Statement, Pristina" published in Bujku on the 16th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I would draw your attention, Mr. Krasniqi, on the Albanian document to -- it appears to be the lower left. And I think this may actually be -- you may actually have a document of this document in the records you brought.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I do have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is this -- is that an article, a report, of the first declaration that you made from Klecka as UCK spokesman on the 15th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And is it an accurate report of what you said on that day in that first declaration that you made?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Honoured Judges, on the 11th, respectively on the 12th of June, 1998, the General Staff appointed me spokesperson of the KLA to communicate with the media in Albanian and at the same time we had -- we were flooded by different media from the world, from Europe and the United States, and up to this time the leaders of the KLA were not known for the public opinion and not known for the soldiers due to the circumstances that I am emphasised earlier, due to the risk and -- existing risk from the secret service of Serbia who had also infiltrated the soldiers and the public. This was the duty and the task of the Serb secret police. However, the public opinion was not directly informed about the personalities that were leading the KLA. In these circumstances, the General Staff appointed me spokesperson of the Kosovo Liberation Army and I accepted this duty wilfully and aware of all the risks that could befall me and my family because all my family members were in the village. I accepted this duty as a person who was already engaged politically against the Belgrade regime. And after informing the public with declaration number 3 from my appointment as a spokesperson on the 13th of June, I gave my first public statement for the Albanian television -- in fact, for that part of the Pristina television that was not able to operate in Pristina but was operating in the frames of the Albanian television in Tirana. This is the declaration, the statement, that I gave in order to inform the Albanians. And in several items I represented -- I presented a part of the programme of the KLA. I consider and I assess that this statement is not a fact, a factive [as interpreted] material that would verify the entire leadership of the KLA. I mentioned earlier that there were circumstances at that time which did not enable us to have control over all those people who were ready to enter war. Out of fear of the regime -- of course I have spoken in the best word about the highest possible level of the organisation of the KLA, but bear in mind that a guerrilla army which was not capable of being not more than three people sometimes, something which went on until the December -- November of 1997 when it was expanded not to a large degree in 1998 because we lacked weapons, we lacked financial means, but we never lacked the readiness to fight the Milosevic regime. We never lacked the readiness, willingness to fight the Serb occupiers despite the risky possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I've hesitated to interrupt you, but you will have opportunities to explain all of these documents. But my question is: Is this document that you have in front of you, the article from Bujku on the 16th of June, 1998, is that an accurate report of what you said in that first statement that you made?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Since I have it with me, I wish to read a sentence from it. "The General Staff of the KLA calls on all the co-nationals, wherever they are, all the freedom fighters to all the experts and professionals of military warfare to respond to the voice of the homeland." This was in fact a call for joining, but it was not an order for people to join, and the KLA has never issued orders to people to join it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: -- because it didn't have the possibility to do that. It just called it to join it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Krasniqi. And we can see where that says that in the document. And that actually brings me to another question which is: When you -- after you became spokesman of the KLA and you gave interviews or made statements to the media, were you speaking on behalf of the General Staff in those statements or were you speaking on behalf of yourself?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I was officially -- I was not officially known to the public as spokesperson to convey the policy of the General Staff of the KLA. I was not -- no longer an individual. I represented and publicised the policy of the General Staff and the KLA at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. There was a little -- I apologise. There was a little problem with the translation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's mistake. It was "I was officially known," not "not officially."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you to the interpreter. I don't need the ask the clarifying question then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Please, if we could go back to this document, the article in Bujku on the 16th of June, 1998. You've read now a sentence about calling on people to join the KLA. Is the rest of the text an accurate account of what you said in your first statement as spokesman of the KLA? And if you could just focus on that question, please, and give me an answer.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Everything I have said here on 16th of June goes to me. I do not claim that I do not -- did not give this statement. I'm not denying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to draw your attention to one sentence in the article. You've already read a sentence. This is a different sentence where it says: "The UCK General Staff is of the opinion that during the present phase, political pluralism is a luxury." Do you see that sentence? It's just before the sentence that you read to us?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes. At that time in Kosova there were many political parties and none of them with the exception I think even though late of the Parliamentary Party of Kosova, had ceased its political activity; while the others, none of them gave up their political activity. And they had become a hurdle to the extension or the growth of the KLA and the assistance given to it. They were fanatically abiding by such -- by some positions which to us were meaningless. At every wartime, even well-organised states usually outlaw -- sorry, disband institutions and concentrate responsibilities on one single body that in many cases substitutes other organisations. Even it disbands parliament. That's why our demand was that even when Kosova was in flames, when the Milosevic regime was committing massacres against civilians, we thought it was more than luxury to be organised in parties and to conduct policy -- politics under the tutelage of Serb regime.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be Prosecution Exhibit P139.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn now to the document at tab 5. And if the witness could be provided with tab 5. This is, for the record, the English is a three of page document which is entitled "UCK Spokesman: Goal is Unification of All Albanians," from the -- from Der Speigel -- from July 6th, 1998, pages 1 to 3. And following it is the three-page translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, do you remember giving an interview to Der Speigel at the beginning of July 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, but I do remember very well that I gave Der Speigel an interview. I gave that interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the report of the interview that appeared in the newspaper in Der Speigel, was it an accurate account of the interview that you had given to the newspaper?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The entire interview, with minor exceptions, is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the minor exceptions, did they pertain to something in particular?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They pertained -- they had a political character. And at that time I didn't think but the way the well-known journalist of Der Speigel wrote about the war and political developments in Kosovo, after the developments in June 1998, I was convinced that she was in a way ordered by the regime, the Serb regime, and that the aim was to give another direction of the policy and the war of the KLA. In that interview I said that the Kosovo Liberation Army was fighting for the unification of the occupied territories and not the way she put it, for greater Albania or something like that. This was the contestation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And aside from that point whether the goal of the KLA was to unify the occupied territories or to create a greater Albania, aside from that point, was the article that appeared in Der Speigel accurate?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the point that you have just referenced about the goal of the KLA, did that cause some controversy after the publication of the article in Der Speigel?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: As I said, on a political plan it did because the aim of the KLA was allegedly to destabilise the entire region of the Balkans. Our war was very transparent. Our requirements might have been minor or greater, but after the consulting we had with the Albanian movement in general as well as with analysts and politicians of the Western world, we concentrated the entire operational activity of the KLA in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this article I want to draw your attention to a question at the -- it's perhaps the -- it's the fourth question. And the newspaper puts a question to you about Rugova. And your answer as translated is: "The policy of the LDK, which is headed by Rugova, has produced only failures over the past 10 years. The Albanians have lost their trust in this policy. Rugova has made too many mistakes." Now, you've addressed this issue at length already, but I wanted to ask you: Did you in fact say that in the interview?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I did tell you during the interview in Pristina that this is what I thought at that time and that my opinion has not changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And then that -- the tenth question. And just to assist you in finding it in your version, it has to do about the UCK central command. And your answer is, and I hope you'll be able to find it in your version is: "The UCK has only one Main Staff and one supreme commander. The military decisions are made here in Kosovo. At the moment, I am the only one permitted to speak on behalf of the UCK." And this topic also has been addressed by you, but I'll just ask you this: Did you say that during the interview?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that. And if needed, we will explain why I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Please do, briefly.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I said this due to the fact that my obligation was to communicate with the public opinion. The fact was that at that time in Kosova it was not known who the person you were communicating with was, and for the -- everybody to give their own opinions, political opinions, and of course at the time this was damaging for the war and caused confusion within the ranks of the KLA and could form confusion within the diplomatic circles of those who were interested in a just war in Kosova. Due to all these risks and many other risks, although we were not prepared and we did know all the precaution measures, the consequences that could be felt from the Serb regime and the collaborators, we did take the risk in order to defend the political aims of the KLA. We did this because we wanted the public, the home and international public, to know the true stand of the KLA and of the struggle led by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now I've just going to ask you about one last question and answer in this interview. It follows -- it's a few after the one we've just been talking about and the newspaper asks: "In the West, the UCK is frequently assessed as a terrorist movement. Why does it kill peaceful Albanians?" And the answer you give according to the document I have is: "Collaborators are warned that we will kill them if they continue to follow the wrong path. However, as an army, we observe all international rules of warfare." And my question is: Did you say this during the interview?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that. And I would like to explain this issue if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You may -- excuse me. You may --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would just ask if you could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, could you please hold one moment; Mr. Whiting is putting something to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you may explain. We just have five minutes until the end of the session and I would just ask if possible if you could provide a brief explanation so we can finish with this document before the end of the session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'd like to be brief. I think that the attempt to argue the fact that the KLA has fought against the Albanians after the war and after the damage incurred by the war is an attempt and a great damage done to our war. We have never aimed at killing Albanians, as you allege. But our -- indeed, the killing or murders were not an aim for us. But this happened at those moments when there was no way out for our people other than that of war. And we fought against the Serb police and army, the violent Serb apparatus that was installed in Kosova. We didn't fight against Albanians, we fought for the Albanians. And today in Kosova each and every one enjoys this reality. More than the KLA -- former KLA members. I believe it's a very serious slander, insult, done to the KLA, to the Albanian people, that we have allegedly fought against the Albanians and not against a violent Serb apparatus. I think that such a practice should come to an end. We as people, Honourable Judges, have never had a problem with justice. As an argument of force, our problem in the course of history has been with the force -- with the force as an argument of justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. Krasniqi, nobody is alleging that the aim of the KLA was to kill Albanians, and you've provided that explanation and I think it's clear in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be Prosecution Exhibit number P140.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I think it would be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, we've come to the end of our day. We have to adjourn now, and because the Judges are engaged in another matter all day tomorrow I'm afraid we can't continue with your evidence until Monday. So we would ask that you return on Monday at 2.15 when your evidence will continue. You'll be given more precise assistance with that by the people assisting you outside. We will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
